title: Proximal Splitting Methods for Hybrid Differentiable Models
claim: Hybrid methods that follow the problem's operator-splitting structure beat solver-only, network-only and prior hybrid baselines across every equation regime.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared legend on top, log-scale bars with error bars
description: A single row of three bar charts, each with a log-scale y-axis labeled Test MSE. The panels are titled Diffusion Only, Reaction Only and Both Terms. A shared legend across the top lists six methods by color: Solver Only (purple), NN Only (brown), SITL (green), SITL+ (blue), HybDR (red, bold, Ours) and HybFB-post (orange, bold, Ours). Black error bars sit on each bar. In every panel, the purple and brown baselines are highest, near 1 to 0.5. The two proposed methods, orange and red, are lowest, near 0.1 and below. SITL+ has very large error bars. In the Reaction Only panel, SITL appears as an empty white bar marked Not Converged. The red bar is the smallest throughout, so the eye goes to the right end of each panel.

abstract: Operator splitting methods are at the foundation of many numerical solvers for partial differential equations. In parallel, unrolled and hybrid learning-based architectures have been introduced to enhance classical solvers, but their design is rarely linked to the underlying problem structure. In this work, we propose a unifying framework that explicitly links operator splitting algorithms from optimization with unrolled hybrid architectures. We show that each operator splitting scheme naturally defines an unrolled architecture, which recovers a wide range of existing plug-and-play and hybrid models as special cases. Using this framework, we design new unrolled hybrid architectures and validate them on benchmark fluid dynamics simulations, where they achieve improved accuracy and stability.
